messages:
Olivia: Pushed a compact guide to the Optimize toolkit focused on short-sequence traffic (prefetch, quant profiles, canary examples). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/908
Ravi: Nice. Can you include a tiny public-safe prefetch helper instead of the internal repo link? Ops flagged private links in docs reviews last week.
Olivia: Yep, I'll paste a minimal helper into the docs examples and reference it. Draft snippet included in the PR.
Ben: Call out that q4_0 and q4_1 can be noisy for very short prompts (<48 tokens). Recommend fp16 fallback or q8_0 for sub-32 traffic.
Olivia: Added a short note and a small tradeoff table comparing q8_0/q4_1/fp16 for <32, 32-128, >128 tokens.
Harper: Also add a conservative canary recipe (5%->20%->50%->100%) and a standard one (10%->40%->100%). Link both to Console alert templates.
Olivia: Done. Included JSON examples for both and the minimal alert query for token alignment: `SELECT sample_id, alignment_score FROM evals WHERE profile='short_seq'` (pseudo).
docs-bot: Reminder created: JIRA-OPT-427 (docs: add public prefetch helper + conservative canary) :bell:
Ravi: Minor nit  the JS example should use BatchClientV1 for SDK <0.10 and BatchClient for >=0.10. Add a compatibility footnote.
Olivia: Added compatibility notes for Python/Go/JS snippets and a tiny migration hint: "if sdk_version < 0.10.0 use legacy batch client".
Ben: Suggest adding this test guidance: "Validate with >=2000 representative prompts; measure p95/p99 latency and exact-match delta before and after."
Olivia: Included a small script in examples to synthesize a 2k prompt set and an evaluation checklist (pre-checks, canary, post-verify).
Harper: I'll do a copyedit and confirm anchors/redirects after Ravi signs off on the quant wording. Plan to merge Thursday if no blockers.
Ravi: I'll review quant text tonight and leave inline comments.
Olivia: Thanks all  will keep the PR open for comments and add the sanitized helper.
